El $R^2$ mide qué parte de la variación: $R^2$ measures what part of the variation in Y the model explains, and the test $t = β̂_1/s(β̂_1)$, with $n − 2$ degrees of freedom, says whether the effect of X is significant.
En el modelo lineal, $β_1$ es el efecto: In the linear model, $β_1$ is the marginal effect: how much Y changes when X rises by one unit. It is what is used, for example, for the marginal propensity to consume in $C = C_0 + c Y_d$.
En el doble logarítmico, $ln Y = β_0 + β: In the double-log model, $ln Y = β_0 + β_1 ln X$, $β_1$ is the elasticity: the percentage change in Y when X rises by 1 %. It is the usual way to estimate demand elasticities or Engel curves.
En el semilogarítmico, $ln Y = β_0 + β_1: In the semi-log model, $ln Y = β_0 + β_1 X$, Y grows at a constant rate: each unit of X multiplies it by $e^{β_1}$. With X in years, $e^{β_1} − 1$ is the annual growth rate.
